CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Strengthening high pressure exiting the northern Great Lakes and building into southern Quebec (~1045 mb) will provide one more dry day today, though easterly winds will be on the increase. Local probabilistic guidance suggests gusts of 25 to 30 mph in the afternoon, with daytime highs remaining near seasonal norms in the low to mid 40s. A strong upper-level wave and PV anomaly descending south through the eastern Plains will merge with the upper-level wave over the western Gulf Coast states, leading to an anomalously deep upper- level trough over the Gulf and Gulf Coast states as the trough axis becomes negatively tilted. Differential cyclonic vorticity advection (DCVA) and strong diffluence aloft ahead of the negatively tilted axis will support robust surface cyclogenesis and a tightening baroclinic zone oriented roughly southwest-to-northeast across the Ohio Valley and lower Great Lakes. An anomalously strong meridional moisture transport plume develops in response to the amplified ridge- trough couplet. Deep tropical and subtropical moisture sourced from both the western Atlantic and the Caribbean Sea is drawn northwestward into the system's warm conveyor belt (WCB). Elevated equivalent potential temperature (theta-e) air and precipitable water (PWAT) values surging well above seasonal climatology will ride up the sloped frontal and isentropic surfaces over Southeast Michigan. Strong low-level jet (LLJ) convergence and deep isentropic ascent favor a broad shield of rain overspreading the CWA by Thursday afternoon into Thursday night, with periods of moderate to potentially locally heavy rain where frontogenetic banding and WCB moisture flux maximize. Total rainfall looks to approach 1 inch across most locations in Southeast Michigan. Euro ensembles even showing a 70 percent chance of 24-hour precipitation amounts reaching at or above 1 inch across the eastern third of the CWA. This rainfall will wipe out much of the extreme rainfall deficit for the month of November, as rainfall totals thus far are only 0.18 inches at Detroit and 0.33 inches at Flint, far below the normal value near 2 inches. Thermal profiles on Thursday are comfortably warm enough to keep precipitation all rain, with daytime highs in the low to mid 40s. As the surface low deepens and tracks northeastward toward the eastern Great Lakes and Saint Lawrence Valley by late Thursday night into Friday, wrap-around cold advection on the back side of the system will cool the column. A transition or brief mix with wet snow remains possible early Friday morning, though marginal surface and boundary-layer temperatures alongside wet ground conditions should limit any accumulation if a changeover even occurs, which looks doubtful as surface dewpoints on Friday look to remain in the mid to upper 30s. Gusty winds are also expected Thursday into Friday as the pressure gradient tightens around the departing cyclone. The strength of the low-level jet and pressure gradient on Thursday suggests easterly wind gusts reaching around 35 mph, while northwest winds on the back side Friday should come in a bit lower due to the lack of strong cold advection. By Saturday, the extreme amplification relaxes as the upper-level trough deamplifies and translates eastward, leaving a cooler, more zonal to weakly cyclonic flow regime across the Great Lakes. Renewed amplification/merger with a strong upper level wave coming out of the Rockies will bring another good shot of appreciable rainfall by the end of the weekend, as low pressure tracks through the Eastern Ohio Valley. A changeover to snow at the tail end Sunday night is not out of the question with the favorable night timing and slightly colder thermal profiles compared to the Thanksgiving storm. && .MARINE... Influence of high pressure decreases today allowing the gradient to tighten, particularly over the southern Great Lakes, leading to an uptick in wind towards 20-25kts for all waters save for northern/north-central Lake Huron. This strengthening onshore flow will bring higher wave action into the Thumb and MI Erie nearshore waters by evening warranting the need for Small Craft Advisories tonight into Thursday. Strong low pressure then lifts out of the Carolinas towards the eastern Great Lakes Thursday-Friday further tightening the local gradient and bringing widespread rain. East to northeasterly gales become possible by Thursday afternoon across Lakes Erie and St Clair with lower but still noteworthy chances (~30- 40%) over the southern Lake Huron basin. As such, Gale Watches have been issued for the southern Great Lakes latter half of the day Thursday into the overnight period. Low pressure gradually peels away from the region over the course of Friday tapering of precip as well as backing winds to the northwest whilst allowing strengths to drop into the 25-30kt range instead. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 637 PM EST Tue Nov 24 2026 AVIATION... The center of broad surface high pressure extends from the Midwest into Lower Mi this evening, and then shifts northward late tonight and Wednesday morning. This brings wind around to an easterly direction across Lake Erie and southern Lake Huron which carries increasing coverage of stratus into Lower Mi. Observations this evening indicate a large area of lake clouds already activated with ceiling around the 3000 ft MVFR/VFR threshold from eastern Lake Huron into central Lake Erie. These clouds are in favorable position to move into Lower Mi as the wind shift develops and increases speed during the late night, first reaching the DTW corridor toward sunrise and spreading north/west toward PTK, FNT, and MBS not long after. The predictability challenge lies in MVFR coverage and duration at onset, then timing of ceiling improvement into VFR as daytime boundary layer growth increases during the morning. This time of year that usually takes until early afternoon, especially toward MBS where clouds linger. Wind gaining gusts near 20 kts pulls dry air in from the central Appalachians which promotes decreasing clouds toward DTW by late morning through Wednesday evening. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * Medium for ceiling at or below 5000 feet from 08-14Z Wednesday. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...Gale Watch from Thursday afternoon through late Thursday night for LHZ421-422. Small Craft Advisory from 7 PM this evening to 7 PM EST Thursday for LHZ441>443. Lake St Clair...Gale Watch from Thursday afternoon through Thursday evening for LCZ460. Michigan waters of Lake Erie...Small Craft Advisory from 1 PM this afternoon to 10 AM EST Thursday for LEZ444. Gale Watch from Thursday morning through Thursday evening for LEZ444. && $$ DISCUSSION...SF MARINE.......KDK AVIATION.....BT You can obtain your latest National Weather Service forecasts online at www.weather.gov/detroit.

A strong upper-level wave and PV anomaly descending south through

This rainfall will wipe out much of the extreme rainfall deficit for
